There is a lot to learn to create beautiful and informative reports using R. In this section, there are several cheatsheets that will hopefully make this learning curve a little easier. 

(If the files are not loading, they are also available on GitHub under the `Cheatsheets` folder [link](https://github.com/PT2412/Warwick-Statistics-Society-R-Course-2026-27).)

# Latex

Latex is a language that allows for additional control over figures, tables and maths. The following is a cheatsheet created by Winston Chang, with the original version available [here](http://wch.github.io/latexsheet/).

# ggplot2

A very popular package for figures is the `ggplot2` package. It can be installed and loaded with the following code (although it is included in the `tidyverse` package).

```{r}
###| ggplot2 package

#install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)
```

![](Cheatsheets/ggplot2.pdf){fig-alt="ggplot2 sheet, A4." width=90% height=500}

## How to use the cheatsheets

Cheatsheets are not a substitute for learning, but they are a fast way to look up functions and syntax while you are coding.

- Use the LaTeX cheat sheet when you need to write mathematical notation, tables, or captions in a report.
- Use the ggplot2 cheat sheet when you are building plots and need to remember common layers such as `geom_point()`, `geom_line()`, and `labs()`.
- Keep the PDF open while you work so you can compare options for themes, scales, and labels.

If a PDF does not display in your browser, download it to your computer and open it with a PDF viewer. Most viewers let you search for keywords such as `aes` or `facet_wrap`, which makes it easy to find the command you need.
